distinguishing_experiment: Compare E1 and E3 at h=0.5 and E2 and E4 at h=2.2. This model predicts equality for each pair because each history has the same sum; E1 versus E5 has sums 1 and 0 and can distinguish the model if p[3] is nonzero.
operation: Replace exponential weighting with the mean of the full recorded history and use it with current drive and elapsed time to predict raw response.
scope: Complete predictive candidate with four shared parameters and no unavailable measurements. It tests a different history summary from R1; neither history sensitivity nor this summary's sufficiency identifies a mechanism.

quantity_annotations.availability: Before response, from the supplied full pre-response history.
quantity_annotations.definition: Arithmetic mean of the recorded history values; for the provided equal-duration intervals this is also the duration-weighted mean.
quantity_annotations.initialization_and_future: Recompute from the history record available before each future response.
quantity_annotations.name: History mean

distinguishing_experiment: Compare E1 and E5 at h=0.5: the first has history mean 0.25 and the second mean 0, while their second moment also differs. E1 and E3 have identical moments through this order and thus are predicted equal. These are prospective formula-based contrasts, not observed outcomes.
operation: Use a nonlinear moment summary of the recorded history, interacting its mean with current drive, as a complete predictive revision.

parameters.name: history second-moment coefficient
parameters.unit: response units per squared dimensionless drive

scope: Complete four-parameter predictor using the recorded history directly. It provides a nonlinear history-summary alternative to R1 and R2. Its predictive performance is untested and it does not identify a physical mechanism.
